This seems really important and useful, and a very good way to start the week. It's much faster than ordinary electrically-based disk drives, and works end-to-end, which is a very important development.

I wonder whether this could be the first iteration of long-term deep storage? The switch from analog to digital is generating an absolutely massive amount of data. It just makes zero sense to keep building power-hungry data centers so we can store data on spinning discs of polished metal. Our current storage schemes have very short lives.

The best thing about this tech is how the mechanism behind the storage allows for more than two states. If this is properly miniaturized, then storage density can become even more ludicrous than SSD's. If a single unit can store an entire byte of information, then, assuming they can get the size down to the size of the units in flash memory, you can get 8x the storage, or a drive 1/8th the size, with read/write speeds theoretically as fast as your processor can handle.

Before we get too excited here, when they say 'permanently' they mean 'potentially decades', not 'forever'. Which is still a nice improvement over CDRs that are unreadable 10-20 years later, but it's hardly etched in the firmament.
